history.new: For every N, the instances y <= N - 2 of x*(y+1) = (x*y)*(x+1) force at most one anchored table (Laver's recursion; written proof in proofs/paper/C17.md). At N = 2^n it is the Laver table A_n, which satisfies the full instance including the wrap-around y = N - 1. For every N <= 4096 (EXP-C17-03, and independently the Skeptic's C program) the full instance has a model exactly at the powers of 2, so for these N left-distributivity of an anchored table is decided by an O(N^2) check.
history.old: For 2 <= N <= 10, an anchored magma satisfies x*(y+1) = (x*y)*(x+1) for all x, y mod N exactly when N is 2, 4 or 8 and the magma is the Laver table; so for these N, left-distributivity of an anchored table is decided by an O(N^2) check.

history.new: Uniqueness for every N: Dehornoy, Braids and Self-Distributivity (2000), Lemma X.1.2; Biane, Sem. Lothar. Combin. 80 (2019) B80c section 2.1 (https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~slc/wpapers/s80biane.pdf). Non-existence of a model of the full instance for N not a power of 2: Biane's footnote 1 ('(2.2) for all p, q ... if N is not a power of 2 this is not true', credited to A. Lewandowski); Aguilera-Iannella (arXiv:2610.06106, 2026) state it as Biane's observation, and it follows from their Prop. 2.5 (the instance at (a, N) holds iff a * N = N) together with Dehornoy's Lemma X.1.7 and Prop. X.1.6. So the statement holds for every N (CLM-C17-08) (Historian audit 2026-10-19, reviews/historian_C11_C20.md).
history.old: Probably a consequence of known Laver-table theory (row N is the identity and p*N = N exactly for powers of 2); not checked against the literature.
